report:
Fresh review of crates.sage_test_harness.compile_tests.query_projection using the current start inputs and captured dependencies. Both implementation entries and both tests are ordinary; there are no TODO/N/A deferrals. I read the complete supplied implementation files and complete annotated test functions rather than relying on previous review output.

The requirements are stable semantic operation names and available identities; retained dynamic parentage, multiplicity and execution/reuse disposition; omission of allocation IDs and temporary paths; sorting only explicitly unordered siblings; visible unknown operations with honest unmapped keys; and use of the Inspector deterministic projection. In sage-host trace.rs, build_dynamic_trace preserves nested nodes through its stack and attach_trace_node, copies QueryLeaf observations, and maps every supplied Salsa disposition directly. Phase/span identities use the semantic operation; unknown queries and external metadata use Unmapped. query_operation strips parenthesized arguments. snapshot_trace replaces unmapped ingredient text with the operation, recurses through children, then normalizes only explicitly unordered children. It does not change the unmapped tag or invent argument identities. Sequential siblings and root order remain intact, and no unknown operation or multiplicity is filtered out. The second associated implementation, observe.rs collect, obtains the event log and serializes this shared typed snapshot as pretty JSON, so the harness uses Inspector semantics rather than raw debug output.

The captured Inspector deterministic_trace claim agrees with those ordering/structure rules. Captured protocol definitions expose stable serde tags, recursively serialized children and dispositions, and observations with default one. These are representation context; the projection logic itself is in the associated trace implementation. Captured CompileTest preparation shows each invocation creates a temporary project and reaches collect with query capture selected, making the independent-project test relevant.

The complete cold_queries_are_stable_across_isolated_projects test prepares identical source independently, compares the full query output, requires executed and body work, and rejects /tmp/ and Id(. Its current additional rendering annotation does not replace or hide these assertions. This provides end-to-end evidence of stable names/output and omission of unstable project/allocation details. The complete query_projection_preserves_structure_and_sorts_only_unordered_siblings test builds a parent with zeta/alpha children, asserts exact root and child counts and parent operation, verifies sequential zeta/alpha versus unordered alpha/zeta, asserts zeta multiplicity three and serialized reused disposition, requires the unmapped tag and operation-only zeta ingredient, and rejects injected Id arguments in serialized output. Alongside the production executed assertion, these assertions cover retained execution/reuse distinctions and unknown-operation visibility. Direct inspection confirms the other available enum dispositions are mapped without collapse. The explicit closed child list catches dropped nodes; the two ordering cases catch accidental sorting of sequential siblings and missing unordered sorting.

Assessment: the current implementation and visible combined assertions account for the complete claim and its qualifications; no necessary edits identified. I executed review start and review read commands during this refresh, but no behavioral test or workspace build. Root is running centralized validation, and no prior test execution is claimed as current execution here. No source edits were made.
